# Simple EM for 2-component Gaussian mixture, compared to 1-Gaussian
def loglik1(x):
    mu = x.mean()
    s = x.std(ddof=0)
    s = max(s, 1e-6)
    return np.sum(-0.5*np.log(2*np.pi*s*s) - 0.5*((x-mu)/s)**2), mu, s

def em2(x, iters=200):
    x = np.asarray(x)
    n = len(x)
    q25, q75 = np.quantile(x, [0.25, 0.75])
    m1, m2 = q25, q75
    s1 = s2 = max(x.std(ddof=0)*0.7, 1e-3)
    w = 0.5
    for _ in range(iters):
        l1 = np.log(w+1e-12) - np.log(s1+1e-12) - 0.5*((x-m1)/s1)**2
        l2 = np.log(1-w+1e-12) - np.log(s2+1e-12) - 0.5*((x-m2)/s2)**2
        mx = np.maximum(l1, l2)
        r1 = np.exp(l1 - mx)
        r2 = np.exp(l2 - mx)
        gamma = r1 / (r1 + r2)
        w = np.clip(gamma.mean(), 1e-3, 1-1e-3)
        m1 = (gamma*x).sum() / gamma.sum()
        m2 = ((1-gamma)*x).sum() / (1-gamma).sum()
        s1 = np.sqrt(max((gamma*(x-m1)**2).sum()/gamma.sum(), 1e-6))
        s2 = np.sqrt(max((((1-gamma)*(x-m2)**2).sum()/(1-gamma).sum()), 1e-6))
    l1 = np.log(w+1e-12) - np.log(s1+1e-12) - 0.5*np.log(2*np.pi) - 0.5*((x-m1)/s1)**2
    l2 = np.log(1-w+1e-12) - np.log(s2+1e-12) - 0.5*np.log(2*np.pi) - 0.5*((x-m2)/s2)**2
    mx = np.maximum(l1, l2)
    ll = np.sum(mx + np.log(np.exp(l1-mx) + np.exp(l2-mx)))
    return ll, {"w": w, "m1": m1, "s1": s1, "m2": m2, "s2": s2}

ll1, mu1, s1 = loglik1(y)
ll2, pars2 = em2(y)
bic1 = -2*ll1 + 2*np.log(len(y))   # k=2
bic2 = -2*ll2 + 5*np.log(len(y))   # k=5
print("\n1-normal:", {"mu": mu1, "sd": s1, "ll": ll1, "bic": bic1})
print("2-normal mixture:", {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in pars2.items()}, "ll", round(ll2, 3), "bic", round(bic2, 3), "delta_bic_1minus2", round(bic1-bic2, 3))

That strongly suggests occasional vial/preparation/outlier contamination in the line measurement process rather than a simple constant bias. Since our deliverable is a process model for lot purity, we need to know whether experimental `y` is the same noisy line readout or close enough to the true lot purity distribution; and for existing lots, re-vialing the same lot can tell us whether vial-specific prep issues occur on lot samples too.
